title: Dog Eat Dog: Balancing Network Effects and Differentiation in a Digital Platform Merger
authors: Chiara Farronato; Jessica Fong; Andrey Fradkin
eligible_reason: Single event (Rover-DogVacay merger announced Mar 2017, DogVacay shut down Jul 2017) common to all markets. Identification uses cross-market variation in premerger Rover share (rover_share_cut bins x year_month, market and month FE), i.e., an exposure-bin DiD with one adoption date. Other main analyses are matched dyadic comparisons and buyer-attrition cross-sections with matching weights. Shipped data are simulated.
design_notes: create_aggregate_data_simulated.R: felm(y ~ rover_share_cut*as.factor(year_month) | market + year_month | 0 | cbsa_seller) on pairs of share bins. matching_dyadic_dvversusrover_simulated.R: feols(y ~ is_dv*i(year_month_clean, ref='2017-02-01') | zip_seller + user_platform + year_month_clean). buyer_attrition_simulated.R: weighted matched cross-sections.
estimators_reported: exposure-bin event study around common merger date
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One merger date; treatment intensity varies by premerger market share.
excluded_specs_summary: All DiD figures/tables: common merger date with continuous or binned exposure (premerger Rover share, DogVacay user status); matching-based attrition regressions.
data_provenance_note: README: simulated dataset 'that has a similar format to the proprietary dataset for Rover'; real data require Rover's cooperation.
screener_notes: Single-date merger design with simulated data.
